root_cause.text: The nf_tables netdev event handlers treated `NETDEV_REGISTER` as a new registration even when the device was already tracked in the hook’s device list (added earlier by `nft_netdev_hook_alloc()`), causing duplicate device registration in `nft_flowtable_event()` and `nft_netdev_event()`.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes the `NETDEV_REGISTER` checks in both `net/netfilter/nf_tables_api.c` and `net/netfilter/nft_chain_filter.c` from `if (!match || (changename && ops)) continue;` to `if (!match || ops) continue;`, and the commit message explicitly says duplicate device registration must be avoided because the device “may have been added by `nft_netdev_hook_alloc()` already when creating the hook.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix flowtable registration logic to skip already registered entries unconditionally on NETDEV_REGISTER.
intent_record.what: In the NETDEV_REGISTER case inside `nft_flowtable_event()`, the condition `if (!match || (changename && ops))` was changed to `if (!match || ops)`, removing the `changename &&` part from the skip check before allocating `struct nf_hook_ops` with `kzalloc_obj()`.
intent_record.how: After this change, any already-registered matching entry (`ops` non-NULL) will be skipped regardless of whether the event is a rename (`changename`) or not. This prevents attempting to register a new hook ops object for an entry that already has one, tightening the registration logic and avoiding duplicate registration paths.

intent_record.intent_summary: Avoid duplicate netdev chain registration by skipping registration whenever ops is already set.
intent_record.what: In the NETDEV_REGISTER case, the condition guarding the registration path was changed from `if (!match || (changename && ops))` to `if (!match || ops)`, removing the `changename &&` part of the `ops` check.
intent_record.how: With this change, any already-initialized `ops` now causes the code to skip the duplicate registration path, regardless of whether the device name changed. This prevents the code from attempting to register a chain more than once when `ops` is already present.

candidates.rationale: This condition only skips registration when the device does not match or when a rename is in progress with existing ops. It fails to treat an already tracked device as already registered on NETDEV_REGISTER, which allows duplicate registration in the flowtable event path.

This pre-fix check has the same flaw: it does not unconditionally skip NETDEV_REGISTER when the netdev is already associated with the hook, so the chain registration logic can register the same device twice.

bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet explicitly adds duplicate-registration avoidance for flowtables. In `nft_flowtable_event()`, the NETDEV_REGISTER path now checks `if (!match || (changename && ops)) continue;`, and the comment says `/* NOP if not matching or already registered */`. This means the device is no longer registered again if it is already present (`ops` found via `ops = nft_hook_find_ops(hook, dev);`). Likewise, the outer notifier now handles `NETDEV_CHANGENAME` separately and invokes `__nf_tables_flowtable_event(NETDEV_REGISTER, dev, true)` followed by a fake unregister, which is part of the fix for rename handling. Since the vulnerable construct was duplicate registration on an already tracked device and the shown code already prevents that, the bug is not present here and the fix is present.
